theme_note: Participants propose something to draw, recruit help, give a location, or announce a mark; proposals vary from a gnome or icon to labels and extra symbols.

second_order: Explaining how r/place and its RuneScape work operated
theme_note: Participants answer what the canvas or image is, explain the five-minute placement rule and collective maintenance, and identify where organizing occurred.

second_order: Celebrating, preserving, and remembering the canvas work
theme_note: Participants celebrate completion, preserve images or re-creations, and retell the RuneScape presence after placement; accounts vary from immediate success to later legacy and nostalgia.

second_order: Announcing and doubting April Fools-day news
theme_note: A documentary announcement is immediately treated as possibly false because of the date; the pair belongs together as announcing and challenging ordinary-looking news.

second_order: Staging and extending April Fools claims
theme_note: Participants announce, embellish, or play along with fake skills, rewards, broadcasts, game modes, and wordplay; the fiction varies from official-looking notices to member-made bait and lyric chains.

second_order: Checking and explaining what was an April Fools trick
theme_note: Participants test surprising claims against dates, interfaces, records, images, or insider explanations and tell others what was fake; checks vary from quick reveals to reconstructing how Clerk was staged.

second_order: Getting fooled and acting on the jokes
theme_note: Participants describe belief producing checking, panic, sleep loss, bankstanding, account recovery, calls to relatives, or disappointment; the consequences range from brief embarrassment to hours of action.

second_order: Praising, tiring of, and policing the joke flood
theme_note: Participants evaluate joke quality and repetition, tell reposts to stop, defend letting others play along, or complain about wasted effort; judgments range from delight to irritation.

second_order: Asking to make joke rewards real
theme_note: Participants turn joke artifacts into feature requests, especially Clerk, capes, hats, and broadcasts, varying the proposed item and reward.

second_order: Crediting and contesting who made the drawings
theme_note: Participants attribute canvas work and control to RS3, OSRS, scripts, or named helpers, while others narrow, correct, or dispute those ownership claims.

second_order: Trying out the subreddit’s April Fools changes
theme_note: Participants encounter, test, explain, and play with altered titles, appended words, banners, fake pixels, and other subreddit-level changes.
Participants ask neighboring groups or RuneScape constituencies for room or assistance and work out borders; responses vary from peace and compromise to refusal and threatened encroachment.

second_order: Building drawings pixel by pixel and by script
theme_note: Participants turn designs into pixels, share or revise scripts, and report construction progress; the means vary between manual placement, multiple accounts, and browser automation.

second_order: Repairing and defending the RuneScape drawings
theme_note: Participants identify damage, call defenders, restore pixels, and keep repair tools running; threats and repair methods vary across the void, other groups, dots, and altered lettering.

second_order: Arguing over calling the canvas work ‘weaponised autism’
theme_note: Participants debate whether the phrase celebrates persistence through self-mockery or demeans autistic people, and ask for different language or greater tolerance.
